title: Doctors Not AI Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on Ways and Means, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Doctors Not AI Act of 2026 aims to keep medical care in the hands of licensed physicians by banning AI systems from diagnosing or treating patients without direct human oversight. The law requires that any AI medical tools be clearly labeled as non-clinical and that all patient‑care decisions remain the responsibility of a qualified doctor.

title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Evaluation Act of 2025
action: Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs. Hearings held.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Risk Evaluation Act of 2025 requires companies to assess the potential risks of AI systems before deployment. It establishes guidelines for reporting, monitoring, and mitigating these risks to protect public safety and privacy.

title: To establish in the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency of the Department of Homeland Security a task force on artificial intelligence, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: This policy establishes a new AI task force within the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency of the Department of Homeland Security. It also contains additional provisions for the agency’s broader responsibilities and operations.

title: CREATE AI Act of 2025
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 29 - 0.
summary: The CREATE AI Act of 2025 is a proposed regulation aimed at governing the development, deployment, and use of artificial intelligence technologies. It seeks to ensure transparency, safety, and accountability while fostering innovation and protecting users from potential risks associated with AI systems.

title: Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on Foreign Affairs, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act proposes a temporary halt on the construction and operation of new AI data centers to address concerns about energy use, environmental impact, and societal effects. It aims to ensure thorough review and planning before expanding AI infrastructure, while encouraging responsible innovation and regulatory oversight.

title: Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, and in addition to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026 establishes regulations to reduce the environmental footprint of AI technologies. It requires developers and users to assess, disclose, and mitigate the energy consumption, resource use, and carbon emissions associated with AI systems.

title: Make AI Work for Americans Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance.
summary: The Make AI Work for Americans Act is proposed legislation that seeks to ensure that the development and deployment of artificial intelligence technologies benefit American citizens. The bill would promote transparency, accountability, and investment in AI research while protecting privacy and fostering economic growth across all sectors.

title: K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions.
summary: The K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026 requires schools to develop and integrate curricula that teach students about artificial intelligence, including its benefits, risks, and responsible use. It also mandates teacher training, establishes federal standards for AI education, and allocates funding to ensure all districts have the resources needed to implement these programs.

title: Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: The Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2026 is a new law designed to make sure that AI systems are safe, accurate, and trustworthy. It establishes guidelines, oversight mechanisms, and research standards so that developers can create AI technology that is reliable and protects public interests.

title: Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2025
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs.
summary: The Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2025 is designed to set strict reliability standards for AI systems, requiring thorough testing, certification, and transparent documentation before deployment. It also establishes federal oversight and allocates funding to support research and development of safe, trustworthy AI technologies.

title: To direct the Secretary of Homeland Security, acting through the Director of the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, to establish a Critical Infrastructure AI Cyber Defense Pilot Program, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: The policy directs the Secretary of Homeland Security to set up a pilot program that uses AI to protect critical infrastructure from cyber threats. The program will develop, test, and evaluate AI-based cyber defense tools and strategies for future deployment.

title: K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 18 - 15.
summary: The K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026 is a legislative initiative designed to embed artificial‑intelligence education into K‑12 curricula so students acquire foundational AI knowledge and digital‑literacy skills. It calls for federal support for teacher training, the development of age‑appropriate AI standards, and resources to help schools and families prepare for a future shaped by AI technologies.

title: VA Claims AI Accountability Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs.
summary: The VA Claims AI Accountability Act is a proposed law that aims to ensure the use of artificial intelligence in processing veterans’ claims is transparent, fair, and subject to oversight. It would establish guidelines and accountability measures to protect veterans’ rights and improve the reliability of AI decision‑making in VA benefits adjudication.

title: VA AI Transparency Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs.
summary: The VA AI Transparency Act of 2026 is a law that requires the Department of Veterans Affairs to openly share how its artificial‑intelligence tools are used, including the data and rules behind those tools. It also sets up rules for regular checks and accountability so veterans and the public can understand and trust the AI decisions that affect their benefits and care.

title: Artificial Intelligence Public Awareness and Education Campaign Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Act aims to raise public awareness about artificial intelligence by launching a national education campaign. It establishes funding, resources, and partnerships to inform citizens about AI benefits, risks, and responsible use.

title: A resolution establishing the Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence.
action: Referred to the Committee on Rules and Administration. (text: CR S5172-5174)
summary: The resolution creates a Select Committee specifically tasked with overseeing the development, use, and regulation of artificial intelligence. The committee will advise lawmakers, assess AI’s impact, and help shape policies to ensure the technology serves the public good while managing risks.

title: A bill to provide for the retraining and support of workers displaced by automation technologies or artificial intelligence, to require Federal action during periods of elevated unemployment, and for other purposes.
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance.
summary: This bill aims to help workers whose jobs are lost to automation or artificial intelligence by providing training programs and support services. It also requires the federal government to take action when unemployment rises sharply, along with other related provisions.

title: A resolution expressing the sense of the Senate regarding the importance of religious freedom, authoritative texts, and transparency in artificial intelligence systems.
action: Submitted in the Senate, considered, and agreed to without amendment and with a preamble by Unanimous Consent. (consideration: CR S4958; text: CR S4951)
summary: The Senate issued a resolution that stresses the need to protect religious freedom and respect authoritative texts in the development and use of artificial intelligence. It also calls for greater transparency in AI systems so that their design, data, and decision‑making processes can be clearly understood and held to account.

title: A bill to establish the Artificial Intelligence Safety Board, and for other purposes.
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The bill proposes creating an Artificial Intelligence Safety Board to oversee the development, deployment, and regulation of AI systems. It also includes additional measures aimed at protecting public safety and ensuring that AI technologies are used responsibly.

title: Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 35 - 0.
summary: This policy aims to shield consumers from misleading or deceptive use of artificial intelligence. It establishes rules and safeguards that require transparency, accurate labeling, and accountability for AI-driven products or services.

title: To direct the Director of National Intelligence to submit to Congress a report on the use of artificial intelligence systems to acquire, analyze, query, disseminate, or otherwise access information under section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act of 1978.
action: Referred to the Committee on the Judiciary, and in addition to the Committee on Intelligence (Permanent Select), for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The directive requires the Director of National Intelligence to submit a report to Congress detailing how artificial intelligence systems are used to acquire, analyze, query, disseminate, or otherwise access information under Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act. The report will outline AI’s role in foreign intelligence operations and inform lawmakers about its use and implications.

title: Artificial Intelligence Education and Workforce Readiness Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Education and Workforce, and in addition to the Committees on Science, Space, and Technology, and Ways and Means, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Education and Workforce Readiness Act of 2026 aims to equip students and workers with the skills needed to thrive in an AI‑driven economy. It proposes new education standards, funding for AI training programs, and initiatives to update workforce development to keep pace with rapid technological change.

title: Open-Source AI Leadership Act
action: Ordered to be Reported by the Yeas and Nays: 26 - 21.
summary: The Open‑Source AI Leadership Act is a proposed law that aims to promote and support the development of AI systems that are built on open‑source software. It seeks to give leaders and innovators the tools and funding they need to create transparent, collaborative AI technologies that benefit society as a whole.

title: Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on the Judiciary, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025 aims to curb the practice of AI firms charging excessively high fees for their services and to prevent them from manipulating wages or salaries of workers. The law would establish regulations and penalties to protect consumers and employees from unfair pricing and wage-setting tactics in the AI industry.

title: A bill to establish the Cybersecurity and AI Board of Investigations, and for other purposes.
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The bill proposes creating a Cybersecurity and AI Board of Investigations to oversee and investigate cyber and artificial‑intelligence risks. It also includes additional measures related to technology oversight and other related matters.
